questions.subject: Excel
questions.prompt: How many journal lines were prepared by Carolyn Slater?

solution.excel: PreparerID is NOT unique: 101 is a different person in each business unit. Look up with both keys: =XLOOKUP([@PreparerID]&"|"&[@BusinessUnitID], PreparerInfo[PreparerID]&"|"&PreparerInfo[BusinessUnitID], PreparerInfo[PreparerName], "Not found").

traps.message: You looked up PreparerID alone. VLOOKUP returns the FIRST 101 it finds (Carolyn Slater), so every 101 line in every business unit was assigned to her. The unique key is PreparerID + BusinessUnitID.

traps.message: A lookup on PreparerID alone always finds something, which hides these exceptions. With the correct two-part key, 148 lines have no valid preparer — an audit finding.

traps.message: '%C%' finds a C anywhere (and LIKE ignores case in SQLite, so every 'c' counts too). 'Starts with' is 'C%'.

questions.subject: SQL

traps.message: COUNT(*) counts every customer. COUNT(Company) counts only the rows where Company is filled in (not NULL).

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many employees were born on a Sunday?

questions.subject: SQL

traps.message: You subtracted calendar years only. That ignores whether the birthday had passed. Use the difference in days / 365.25.
You computed age today, not age at the hire date.

questions.prompt: How many downloads at the $0.99 price have happened?

traps.message: You counted tracks in the catalogue. Downloads are sales, which are in InvoiceLine.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: How many tracks have been downloaded the maximum number of times (i.e. are tied for most downloads)?

solution.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT TrackId, SUM(Quantity) AS n FROM InvoiceLine GROUP BY TrackId)
WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT SUM(Quantity) AS n FROM InvoiceLine GROUP BY TrackId));

traps.message: That's the number of tracks downloaded at least once. Find the maximum downloads per track, then count tracks at that maximum.
That's the maximum number of downloads (2), not the number of tracks that reached it. 'Top 5' would be misleading here: hundreds of tracks are tied.

questions.subject: SQL

solution.sql: SELECT julianday(MAX(InvoiceDate)) - julianday(MIN(InvoiceDate)) FROM Invoice;

traps.message: Subtracting the date text gives the difference in years only (2013 - 2009). Convert with julianday() to get days.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: An album counts as downloaded when ALL its tracks appear on a single invoice. How many distinct albums have been downloaded?

solution.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.AlbumId) FROM Album a
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  WHERE t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT il.TrackId) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Track t2 WHERE t2.AlbumId = a.AlbumId));

traps.message: You counted albums with at least one track sold. Under the stated definition, all the album's tracks must be on the same invoice.

You counted complete-album purchases (invoice + album pairs). Some albums were bought on more than one invoice, so count DISTINCT AlbumId. (The PwC answer sheet reports 49, which is this purchase count.)

questions.note: Every album that qualifies has only one track, so the definition is weaker than it sounds.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: What is the most popular genre (by tracks sold)?

solution.sql:
SELECT g.Name FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name ORDER BY SUM(il.Quantity) DESC LIMIT 1;

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: List every invoice billed to Germany with the customer's full name, the invoice date and the invoice total. How many invoices are there?

solution.sql:
SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS Customer, i.InvoiceDate, i.Total FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
WHERE i.BillingCountry = 'Germany' ORDER BY i.InvoiceDate;

traps.message: You listed both tables without a join condition (a cross join), so every invoice was paired with every customer. Join ON CustomerId.
